sand.definition: Small loose grains of rock or mineral material.

ocean.definition: A large body of water constituting a principal part of the hydrosphere.

wave.definition: One of a series of ridges that moves across the surface of a liquid (especially across a large body of water).

shore.definition: The land along the edge of a body of water.

cliff.definition: A steep wall of rock or earth.

dune.definition: A ridge of sand created by the wind.

tide-pool.definition: A small pool of seawater left among rocks when the tide goes out.
tide-pool.exampleUsage: Small shells were visible in the tide pool.

horizon.definition: The range of interest or activity that can be anticipated.

reef.definition: A submerged ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the water.

cove.definition: Small or narrow cave in the side of a cliff or mountain.

bay.definition: An indentation of a shoreline larger than a cove but smaller than a gulf.

lagoon.definition: A body of water cut off from a larger body by a reef of sand or coral.

towel.definition: A piece of absorbent cloth used for drying your body or other things.

sunscreen.definition: A cream spread on the skin.

umbrella.definition: A covering used to protect someone from rain.

beach-chair.definition: A portable outdoor seat that folds for carrying, made from a wooden frame stretched with canvas.

cooler.definition: An insulated container used to keep food and drinks cold.

flip-flops.definition: Open sandals with a flat sole held by a Y-shaped strap between the toes.
flip-flops.exampleUsage: She wore flip-flops on the sand.

sunglasses.definition: (plural) spectacles that are darkened or polarized to protect the eyes from the glare of the sun.

hat.definition: An informal term for a person's role.

swimsuit.definition: Tight fitting garment worn for swimming.

bikini.definition: An atoll in the Marshall Islands.

swim-trunks.definition: Shorts designed to be worn by boys or men for swimming.
swim-trunks.exampleUsage: He changed into swim trunks at the beach.

goggles.definition: (plural) tight-fitting spectacles worn to protect the eyes.

snorkel.definition: Breathing device consisting of a bent tube fitting into a swimmer's mouth and extending above the surface.

fins.definition: To show the fins above the water while swimming.

swimming.definition: Moving through water for exercise or pleasure.

surfing.definition: The sport of riding a surfboard toward the shore on the crest of a wave.

diving.definition: An athletic competition that involves diving into water.

kayaking.definition: The activity of traveling on water in a kayak; safe participation depends on conditions, flotation equipment, and appropriate supervision.
kayaking.exampleUsage: The beach program offered supervised kayaking in a designated area.

paddleboarding.definition: The activity of standing or kneeling on a large board and moving across water with a paddle; safety depends on conditions and supervision.
paddleboarding.exampleUsage: The beach center offered supervised paddleboarding.

boogie-boarding.definition: Riding waves while lying or partly kneeling on a small bodyboard.
boogie-boarding.exampleUsage: Children used bodyboards only in the lifeguarded swimming area.

jet-skiing.definition: The activity of riding a powered personal watercraft; it is age- and license-restricted in many places and requires compliance with local safety rules.
jet-skiing.exampleUsage: The sign states that jet-skiing is restricted to eligible operators under local rules.

sailing.definition: The activity of flying a glider.

windsurfing.definition: The equipment for windsurfing includes the board, sail, mast, boom, fittings, rig, and related gear.

water-skiing.definition: A water sport in which a person is pulled across the water on skis by a powered boat; it requires trained supervision and safety equipment.
water-skiing.exampleUsage: The resort advertises water-skiing only through supervised professional operators.

fishing.definition: Catching fish as a sport or activity.
fishing.exampleUsage: The fishing was identified during the lesson.

sandcastle.definition: A miniature castle built by shaping and compressing sand, usually on a beach for recreation or artistic display.

frisbee.definition: A flat flying disc thrown between people.

volleyball.definition: An inflated ball used in playing volleyball.

sunbathing.definition: Describes activities, routines, or equipment connected with sunbathing, tanning, or outdoor exposure to ultraviolet radiation, the sun’s high-energy rays.

picnic.definition: Eating a meal outdoors, often on a blanket or table.

kite-flying.definition: The activity of controlling a lightweight kite held by a line in the wind.
kite-flying.exampleUsage: The family flew a small kite in an open area away from roads and power lines.

shell-collecting.definition: The hobby or study of gathering mollusc shells and learning about them.

barbecue.definition: To cook outdoors on a barbecue grill.

bonfire.definition: A large outdoor fire that is lighted as a signal or in celebration.

reading.definition: Looking at words in a book or other text.

walking.definition: Moving on foot at a steady pace for exercise or travel.

jogging.definition: Moving on foot faster than walking.
jogging.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "jogging" in an educational description.

seagull.definition: Mostly white aquatic bird having long pointed wings and short legs.
seagull.exampleUsage: The seagull was identified during the lesson.

crab.definition: A stroke of the oar that either misses the water or digs too deeply.

starfish.definition: Echinoderms characterized by five arms extending from a central disk.

jellyfish.definition: Large siphonophore having a bladderlike float and stinging tentacles.

dolphin.definition: Large slender food and game fish widely distributed in warm seas (especially around Hawaii).
dolphin.exampleUsage: The dolphin was identified during the lesson.

sea-turtle.definition: Large turtles that spend most of their lives in tropical or subtropical oceans come ashore mainly to lay eggs on sandy beaches.

pelican.definition: Large long-winged warm-water seabird having a large bill with a distensible pouch for fish.
pelican.exampleUsage: The pelican was identified during the lesson.

seahorse.definition: Small fish with horse-like heads bent sharply downward and curled tails.
seahorse.exampleUsage: The seahorse was identified during the lesson.

clam.definition: Burrowing marine mollusk living on sand or mud.

coral.definition: The hard stony skeleton of a Mediterranean coral that has a delicate red or pink color and is used for jewelry.

seaweed.definition: Plant growing in the sea, especially marine algae.

sea-urchin.definition: A small round marine animal with a hard shell covered in movable spines.
sea-urchin.exampleUsage: A sea urchin was visible between the rocks.

lifeguard.definition: An attendant employed at a beach or pool to protect swimmers from accidents.

lifeguard-tower.definition: An elevated station from which lifeguards watch a beach or swimming area.
lifeguard-tower.exampleUsage: The lifeguard tower overlooked the swimming zone.

warning-flag.definition: A colored flag used to communicate beach or water-safety conditions.
warning-flag.exampleUsage: Visitors checked the warning flag before entering the water.

first-aid-kit.definition: A portable set of medical supplies and equipment provides immediate help for minor injuries or sudden illness while professional care is unavailable.

shower.definition: A place or device that sprays water over you so you can wash your body.

changing-room.definition: A private room or cubicle where people change clothes.
changing-room.exampleUsage: The beach facility has a changing room.

boardwalk.definition: A walkway made of wooden boards.

pier.definition: A platform built out from the shore into the water and supported by piles.

parking-lot.definition: An area with marked spaces where vehicles can be parked.
parking-lot.exampleUsage: The beach parking lot fills early on weekends.

trash-can.definition: A container that holds waste until it is removed.
